transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-02 16:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Lydia Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Hannah Kim (CTO - StratoMed), Miles Ortega (Platform Eng), Priya Narang (ML Eng)

Summary: Quick recap of the last 48 hours of throughput runs. Focus on continuous batching parameters, concurrency caps, and queueing/backpressure behavior during bursts. Agreed to small-window batching and lower concurrency cap to reduce tail latency; validate with a 2-hour soak.

00:00:03 Lydia: alright folks thanks for hopping on, we'll kick off, quick agenda — run telemetry review, proposed retune, plan soak, next steps. Samir, you want to take us through the dashboards?
00:00:12 Samir: yeah sure, i'll share the perf sheet. so over the last 48 hours we ran three 30-minute ramps; what you see on p95 is the tail spikes correspond with 50 to 80 rps bursts and queue depth rising from 4 to ~28, so the runtime started creating backpressure which pushed latency to the 600 to 900ms band intermittently.
00:00:39 Hannah: those spikes were visible in our app too, users saw timeouts at the client layer. we budgeted sub-500ms 95th for the demo.
00:00:48 Samir: got it. two levers we tuned: continuous batching.window_ms and concurrency.cap. Previously we had window_ms 30 and concurrency.cap 28 per GPU slice. That gave good throughput but long tail when bursty traffic pushed queue depth high.
00:01:05 Miles: can you remind me — when you say concurrency.cap that's per-process or per-GPU?
00:01:09 Samir: good question. per serving shard, so effectively per GPU instance, yes. lowering it will reduce active inflight tokens and keep KV cache warm for more requests, but you'll drop steady throughput a bit.
00:01:21 Priya: and what about prefix/KV cache hit rates? we saw some churn because sequence lengths vary across requests.
00:01:26 Samir: right, cache hit was about 72% in these runs. when concurrency is high we evict more often, so shorter window but lower hits. our recommendation: small window_ms ~15-20ms + lower cap to keep hit rate above 70% while reducing tail.
00:01:43 Lydia: to be clear on goals — for the pilot we want p95 under 350-400ms for demo traffic and steady cost increase under 8%. is that still the target?
00:01:52 Hannah: yes, and important: we can't exceed our SOC2 constraints and data must stay in our VPC, so any perf profiling or log pull needs to be scoped.
00:02:02 Lydia: understood. Samir — walk us through the new telemetry thresholds you propose.
00:02:06 Samir: sure. baseline: p50 ~60ms, p95 target 350, p99 under 900. queue_depth alarm at 18, if we hit 18 for >30s we start shedding via cheaper model fallback and trigger autoscaler to add burst nodes if allowed. We'll also add a backpressure metric and maintain a 10-second moving average — if avg response time jumps 2x we start activating queue shedding policies.
00:02:30 Miles: on the fallback model — that's in another project for us. how transparent is the routing? will responses switch models mid-session?
00:02:37 Samir: by default we route by request and leave session affinity off for safety; you can enable session affinity but then you'd keep the same model. Fallback is stateless per-request to a smaller LLM variant; we include a header in the response so you can detect it.
00:02:50 Priya: will the small variant impact hallucination rates? we need to monitor quality metrics closely.
00:02:54 Samir: absolutely — Priya, that's why we want your eval job on the soak outputs. if we see drift beyond the threshold we'll adjust the shed behavior and maybe prefer throttling over fallback for certain endpoints.
00:03:05 Hannah: can you also show the cost delta? our CFO asked what the worst-case month looks like for burst capacity.
00:03:10 Lydia: i have a quick slide — steady-state cost is X, with burst autoscale to 2x it's roughly +24% on token compute; with fallback-only it can be +6% but higher risk to output quality. We'll attach the spreadsheet after the call.
00:03:24 Miles: one more constraint — our infra team requires KMS-integrated keys and audit logs for model inputs for compliance. Are those payload logs redacted by default?
00:03:33 Samir: Redwood supports KMS + HSM integrations for Private deployments; for hosted POC we offer encrypted streams and we can redact tokens at ingestion. We'll submit the SOC2/compliance note.
00:03:45 Hannah: good. ok, let's talk specifics of the retune so we can test quickly.
00:03:49 Samir: Proposed change set: batching.window_ms from 30 -> 18, continuous batching.max_batch_size keep at 64, concurrency.cap from 28 -> 18; queue_depth alarm lowered to 18; fallback model route enabled for specific endpoints (summary generator only). Also toggled prefix cache TTL to 120s from 60s for stabilized sequences.
00:04:12 Priya: TTL to 120s — interesting, because some of our requests have a long gap between follow-ups, could that cause stale context?
00:04:18 Samir: TTL only affects cached KV entries lifecycle; if requests are sparse it won't hurt, it'll just keep entries warmed for 2 minutes. We can instrument cache miss rate and adjust.
00:04:27 Miles: what's the plan for the soak? timeline and telemetry ingestion?
00:04:31 Lydia: plan is Samir pushes config to staging by EOB tomorrow, run a 2-hour soak starting 09:00 PT 2026-09-04 using production-like traffic replay. Priya runs evals in parallel. Miles provides RBAC token for telemetry; Lydia shares the runbook and spreadsheet.
00:04:48 Hannah: i want a mid-soak check at +60 minutes to confirm p95. If it's still bad we abort and revert.
00:04:55 Samir: yep we'll put automated checks that will stop the soak if p95 > 600 for 10 minutes straight.
00:05:03 Priya: small note — our dataset has longer sequences for certain customers, we'll flag endpoints that should be excluded from aggressive fallback to avoid degraded UX.
00:05:11 Samir: noted. we'll add an exclusion list per route.
00:05:16 Lydia: any blockers on RBAC or logs? Miles?
00:05:19 Miles: i'll get the token to Samir and will open telemetry stream to the 'redwood-debug' project. need to confirm retention window; we prefer 30 days but can do 7 for the POC.
00:05:29 Hannah: also send procurement the SOC2 scoping note. we may need an NDA amendment for audit logs.
00:05:36 Lydia: will do.
00:05:38 [5:30 silence while Samir shares screen and they step through graphs]
00:06:10 Samir: showing the ramp 3 plot — you can see how the queue depth climbs at the 12:40 mark. note that KV eviction correlates tightly with concurrency above 22.
00:06:22 Priya: is eviction measurement reliable? sometimes the parser shows noisy values.
00:06:26 Samir: the metric is sampling-based but we've correlated it with internal counters; it's accurate within +/- 3%.
00:06:32 Hannah: okay i'm comfortable with the plan. the main ask is we don't regress quality. Priya will sign off.
00:06:39 Lydia: perfect. quick logistics — Samir will run the soak, upload logs to the shared drive, Priya runs eval, Miles grants tokens. Follow-up sync wednesday to review soak. Anything else?
00:06:52 Miles: Can we get a short checklist for rollback? If the soak fails we want an explicit revert procedure.
00:06:57 Samir: yes, push pre-baked rollback playbook to the staging cluster; we'll tag the previous config and run the revert script. I'll include that in the runbook.
00:07:06 Hannah: one last question — if we enable fallback-only policy instead of autoscale, is there a rapid way to toggle autoscale on if we see quality issues?
00:07:14 Samir: yes, autoscale is a flag on the routing policy; the ops toggle flips within ~30s to 2 minutes depending on cluster spin-up. We'll document that.
00:07:23 Lydia: great. closing notes: Lydia to send runbook + cost sheet; Samir to push config + run soak; Priya to eval outputs; Miles to supply token; follow-up 2026-09-07. Thanks everyone.
00:07:36 Hannah: thanks all.
00:07:38 [meeting ends, participants drop]
